steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Combine blackberries, sugar, cinnamon, and nutmeg in a bowl until evenly blended. Spread evenly into the prepared baking dish.
Place cake mix in a separate bowl. Mix in butter until crumbly; sprinkle evenly over top of berries.
Bake in the preheated oven until the mixture is bubbly, and the topping is golden brown, 40 to 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Wendy's Easy Blackberry Cobbler
raw_recipe.description: This simple blackberry cobbler is topped with cake mix and butter for an easy way to use those abundant blackberries found in the hot summer months!
raw_recipe.name: Wendy's Easy Blackberry Cobbler

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Combine blackberries, sugar, cinnamon, and nutmeg in a bowl until evenly blended. Spread evenly into the prepared baking dish.
Place cake mix in a separate bowl. Mix in butter until crumbly; sprinkle evenly over top of berries.
Bake in the preheated oven until the mixture is bubbly, and the topping is golden brown, 40 to 45 minutes.

review.reviewBody: I made this with a couple changes. I did not add nutmeg, used butter instead of margarine.I also added more sugar since my berries weren't that sweet. I didn't need to, as the crust is also sweet. It came out tasty, but too runny. I will make this again but I will add cornstarch to the dry ingredients to thicken. Very easy to make, since you don't have to make crust !

This recipe only works if you turn the blackberries into "pie filling" first. Combine 2 pints blackberries with 3/4 cup sugar and heat over low until sugar is melted, about 5 min. Will be runny. Then combine 3 tbsp cornstarch with 3 tbsp water and add to mixture. Bring it to a boil to activate the starch while stirring. It should thicken up. Remove it to a bowl to cool down to warm, then stir in about a tsp of lemon zest. From there you can transfer it to a pan, sprinkle the yellow cake mix over it, cut up a stick of real butter over the yellow cake mix and bake at 350 or 45 min or until golden. I've done this for years and it comes out right every time. Hope this helps you!

I like my cobbler a little thicker and not so sweet, so I used 8 cups berries 1/2 C flour, 1/2 C sugar and 1 tsp. cinnamon. I made the topping as directed but if you want to cut calories it is perfectly fine if you halve the topping. This got rave reviews from the family. I mixed up the rest of my berries with the flour and sugar and packed them to freeze 4 cups in a bag so I can make smaller versions of this all winter for just my husband and I.

Couple changes made
Used brown sugar: butter instead of margarine: added 3 teaspoons cornstarch to cake mix
Baked 45 min
Came out perfect 
Consistently was perfect and delicious

I made this recipe using peaches instead of berries. I used canned peaches and did not heat them before baking. I just put them in a bowl and add cinnamon i little sugar to taste and a teaspoon or so of flour. mix well. Add the cake mix mixture by the teaspoon. and baked. Came out fantastic. I love this recipe.

The berries are not yet in season, so I used frozen blueberries, raspberries and blackberries carefully thawing them on paper towels. I did not want them mushy, so I carefully put them in the pan. I added almost 1/3 cup of sugar and a bit more cinnamon. I kept the topping the same and my husband loved it!!!! Delicious!!!!

I made it with blackberries, red raspberries and blueberries...it was quite tasty but I reduced the sugar to 1 1/4 cups and for me, it was still too sweet. My guests loved it. Next time I will reduce the sugar again to 1 cup and I think it will be perfect. Served with vanilla ice cream.

Made this last night and it was wonderful.. I cut the sugar by 1/cup and added lemon zest to the berry mixture along with some Vanilla extract and some cornstarch.. turned out great.. fun desert and easy to make..
I had numerous fresh mixed berries. They were sweet, so I sprinkled some sugar in them and added a tablespoon of cornstarch. Turned out amazing! So easy.
I used less sugar, 1 cup instead of 1-1/2 and it was plenty sweet. We liked it very much and would make it again next time blackberries are on sale.

Made this with 5 6oz packs of fresh blackberries and with betty crocker lemon cake mix. It was good, but definitely sweet I'd recommend cutting the sugar in half. I also plan to try with a vanilla cake mix next time. If it's too sweet, I'll plan to have vanilla ice cream or cool whip available.

I added minute tapioca to thicken the juices. I had 8 cups of berries so I used 8 cups. Used freshly grated nutmeg, no cinnamon. Butter of course with the cake mix . Heavy cream whipped with a little sugar and some sour cream blended into the whipped cream. Also about a third of a cup of lemon juice into the berries. Haven't made better.
No changes

I made this recipe as is. My berries were frozen from a store and then thawed. Most of the berries were very green so it needed all the sugar. I was not looking for a cobbler with a crumbly crust on the top of the berries. However, the toping was sweet enough to blend with the sour berries and made a good combination. Still not what I wanted and I am still looking for a good cobbler.

I made it frozen mixed berries and it turned out delicious. I would add less sugar. My family loved it but also said it was a bit sweet. I’m going to make with 1 cup of sugar instead of 1 1/2 cups. I made for desert on Thanksgiving and was asked to make it for Christmas.
This was super easy. For me, it was a little too sweet. I’ll make it again and use just a bit less sugar in the berries.
I used lemon cake mix instead of yellow
I made it, but used 1 cup of sugar instead of a cup and a half. Also used butter instead of margarine. Everyone loved it. Was easy to make!
It was a hit! I will definitely make it again.

I made this with blueberries and pineapple instead of blackberries. I also made one with gluten free cake mix and one with regular cake mix. Only thing I would change is the amount of sugar. It definitely need need as much as the recipe called for. I will make it again, with less sugar!
